standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of a tensor product along the completion modulo powers of the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma identifying the tensor product of the completion with the base modulo the powers of the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the quotients of the tensor product ring appearing in the computation of the nth powers of the prime ideals.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case (proof lines 2969-2973): one may assume the scheme is affine and hence given by a ring B, with the base change given by the tensor product of B with the completion.

Compare the powers of the primes (proof lines 2973-2994): for every n the quotient of the tensor product ring by the nth power of the extended maximal ideal equals the quotient of B by the nth power of the maximal ideal; since the maximal ideal of the base is contained both in the prime of B and in the prime of the tensor product ring, the n-th powers of those primes have quotient rings which are both quotients of that same ring, which gives the isomorphism of the completions.
proof_roadmap: Assume the scheme is affine and write the base change as a tensor product.
Identify the quotients of the tensor product by the powers of the extended maximal ideal.
Conclude the isomorphism of the completions of the two local rings.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a scheme over a local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal, the local ring of a point of the base change to the completion and the local ring of its image have isomorphic completions (statement lines 2965-2972). The proof (proof lines 2973-2994) reduces to an affine situation and compares the quotients by the powers of the relevant prime ideals. H2: a complete short computation.
